road.title: At the restaurant
road.description: A thin, anxious presence in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, next to a small bell marked RING FOR ATTENTION and a larger one marked DO NOT. Mungo is a Chef of the Old Recipe and follows it to the letter, although several of the letters have worn away.

openObjectives.prompt: Mungo is guarding a large book in which, it appears, tables are kept. Tell Mungo that you would like to book a table, using Italian.
Tell Mungo what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Mungo asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Mungo that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

character.name: Mungo Tallow
character.description: A thin, anxious presence in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, next to a small bell marked RING FOR ATTENTION and a larger one marked DO NOT. Mungo is a Chef of the Old Recipe and follows it to the letter, although several of the letters have worn away.

npc.narrative: Sotto le stelle, the Reluctant Thicket has put out one candela and a sign that says aperto, though not which way. Mungo Tallow stands first in a fila of one, holding a menù and a small barattolo marked cappello. He sees you and straightens, like a man who has waited all giorno.
npc.native: Buonasera, buonasera! Io sono Mungo, e questo è il mio ristorante. Qui, di sera, è bene prenotare: io prenoto sempre, anche per una persona. Che cosa vuoi fare stasera?
npc.translation: Good evening, good evening! I am Mungo, and this is my restaurant. Here, in the evening, it is good to book: I always book, even for one person. What do you want to do tonight?

player: Buonasera Mungo! Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per due, per favore. Io e il mio amico abbiamo molta fame.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Mungo, booked a table for two and even said you and your friend are very hungry, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you correctly said you would like to book a table with "Vorrei prenotare un tavolo".

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Vorrei prenotare un tavolo per due

objectiveResults.feedback: You haven't said yet what you will have to start with; Mungo will ask again later.
You haven't said yet that the food is cold or too salty; this will come up again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Mungo what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Mungo asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Mungo that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Mungo writes your name in a large libro with a very short matita, poi joins the fila in front of the tavolo, da solo. Above the roof the stelle are out, and on the counter a tin marked cappello waits to be filled.
npc.native: Un tavolo per due, benissimo! Molta fame è una buona notizia per il mio cappello. Il prosciutto è ottimo come antipasto, e la pasta è ottima come primo. Che cosa prendi tu?
npc.translation: A table for two, very good! A lot of hunger is good news for my hat. The ham is excellent as a starter, and the pasta is excellent as a first course. What will you have?

player: Per cominciare prendo il prosciutto, grazie. E il mio amico prende la bruschetta. Perché il cappello?

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work: you ordered the ham, ordered the bruschetta for your friend, and even asked Mungo about his hat, all in good Italian! Next, try naming the course with the starter phrase.

objectiveResults.feedback: Your Italian is correct and you ordered the ham, but this task wants the phrase for a starter: try "Come antipasto prendo il prosciutto."
Not needed yet: later, when the food arrives, tell Mungo that it is cold or too salty. Mungo will ask again then.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Mungo what you will have to start with, using Italian.
Mungo asks whether everything is all right, in the voice of someone who expects it to be. Tell Mungo that the food is cold, or too salty, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Mungo taps a tin on the bancone, marked cappello in careful lettere. It rattles like a very piccola fortuna. Fuori, a queue of one waits by the porta under le stelle, and Mungo nods at it as at an old customer.
npc.native: Prosciutto e bruschetta: perfetto! Sono buoni come antipasto, e la pasta è buona come primo. Il cappello è un sogno, e ogni cliente aiuta. E tu, che cosa prendi come primo?
npc.translation: Ham and bruschetta: perfect! They are good as a starter, and the pasta is good as a first course. The hat is a dream, and every customer helps. And you, what will you have as a first course?

player: Come antipasto prendo il prosciutto, e poi la pasta. Mmm... scusa, ma il prosciutto è troppo salato!

verdict.overallFeedback: Bravo! You ordered your starter and your pasta, then politely complained that the ham was too salty, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Come antipasto prendo il prosciutto" is a natural way to say what you'll have to start.
Well done: "il prosciutto è troppo salato" clearly tells Mungo the food is too salty.

npc.narrative: You push the piatto piano away. Mungo leans over the tavolo, molto pallido, like a man hearing his own name read out in tribunale. Under the stelle a fila of one waits by the porta, and it is him.
npc.native: Troppo salato? Mi dispiace tanto! La ricetta è antica, e la lettera del sale è quasi sparita. Che cosa mangi di solito a casa?
npc.translation: Too salty? I am so sorry! The recipe is old, and the letter for the salt has almost disappeared. What do you usually eat at home?

player: A casa mangio spesso il riso con le verdure. Non cucino bene! E la pasta, è salata anche?

npc.narrative: Under the stelle, Mungo leans over the bancone and copies your answer onto a modulo with a very short matita. Behind him, a queue of one (himself) shuffles forward, perfettamente in ordine. From the cucina comes a smell of sale, mostly.
npc.native: Il riso con le verdure è un ottimo piatto! La pasta non è salata, no: è perfetta. Stasera faccio la fila da solo, per essere pronto. Chi cucina di solito a casa tua?
npc.translation: Rice with vegetables is an excellent dish! The pasta is not salty, no: it is perfect. Tonight I am queuing on my own, to be ready. Who usually cooks at your house?

player: Cucino io, ma male. Il mio amico dice che la mia pasta è come la gomma. Tu hai imparato la ricetta da chi?

npc.narrative: La notte is clear, and the stelle hang over the tavolo like a bill nobody has paid. Mungo opens a very old libro on the counter, which has more gaps than pages, and reads from it with great confidence.
npc.native: Ho imparato la ricetta da un libro molto vecchio, ma ci sono poche lettere. La gomma? Il tuo amico è sincero, e un cliente così è un tesoro per il mio cappello. Lui cucina meglio di te?
npc.translation: I learned the recipe from a very old book, but there are few letters. Rubber? Your friend is honest, and a customer like that is a treasure for my hat. Does he cook better than you?

player: No, lui non cucina mai, lui mangia solo! Va bene, il conto per favore. Arrivederci!

npc.narrative: Mungo hurries to the cassa and writes the conto on a slip, then stands in a fila behind himself to wait his turn. Above the strada the stelle are out, and the lanterna by the door flickers politely.
npc.native: Lui mangia solo? Che bel mestiere! Ecco il conto: per il cappello è una buona sera. Che cosa fate dopo cena, tu e il tuo amico?
npc.translation: He only eats? What a fine trade! Here is the bill: for the hat it is a good evening. What do you and your friend do after dinner?
